problem_statement:
ENH: Improve performance of reductions like ``np.sum``

### Proposed new feature or change:

We can improve performance of reductions like `np.sum()` which are much more expensive than normal ufunc operations:
```
x = np.array([1., 2., 3.])
%timeit np.abs(x)
%timeit np.sum(x)
```
Results in:
```
288 ns ± 0.701 ns per loop (mean ± std. dev. of 7 runs, 1,000,000 loops each)
1.48 μs ± 2.17 ns per loop (mean ± std. dev. of 7 runs, 1,000,000 loops each)
```
Some prototyping shows we improve performance by a factor of 2 (at least for the contiguous case), see  https://github.com/numpy/numpy/compare/main...eendebakpt:numpy:ufunc_reduction_performance.

[Bug]: SSH helpers hard-code a Unix-only ssh path

## Summary

A local code audit found that SSH helpers assume `/usr/bin/ssh`, which breaks on hosts where a trusted SSH client exists in a platform-specific location, such as Windows OpenSSH.

## Affected area

- `src/infra/ssh-config.ts`
- `src/infra/ssh-tunnel.ts`

## Repro

On a Windows host with the built-in OpenSSH client installed in the Windows OpenSSH location, call the SSH config/tunnel helpers. They try `/usr/bin/ssh` instead of resolving the platform SSH executable.

## Expected

SSH helpers should resolve a trusted SSH binary using the repository's system-binary resolution conventions and return a clear diagnostic when none is available.

memory-core: MMR diversity re-ranking does O(n³) work and blocks the event loop for minutes on broad searches over large corpora

**Summary**

With `hybrid.mmr.enabled=true`, a broad `memory_search` (`corpus=all`) over a mature corpus can synchronously seize the gateway event loop for 2–5 minutes at ~100% CPU. During the seizure every gateway function is frozen — channels, heartbeats, RPC — and the search's own 75s timeout cannot fire, because the timer lives on the same starved loop. In our reproductions the timeout result surfaced ~212 seconds after the timeout nominally expired.

**Environment**

- OpenClaw 2026.7.1 (`release/2026.7.1`), Node 25.9.0, macOS (Apple Silicon)
- Memory corpus: 32,839 chunks (~1 year of single-user usage)
- `hybrid.mmr.enabled: true`, `lambda: 0.5`

The affected code path is unchanged on current `main` (`extensions/memory-core/src/memory/mmr.ts`).

**Reproduction**

1. Mature corpus (tens of thousands of chunks).
2. `memory_search` with `corpus=all`, `maxResults=10`, `minScore=0.2`, and a query of common words (e.g. `creative courage connection audience understanding`). Rare-phrase queries often do NOT trigger it — candidate-pool size is the driver. When session results are included, `corpus=all` expands the tool's requested `maxResults` from 10 to a bounded manager request of 200; the manager can then request up to 200 candidates from each retrieval branch before hybrid fusion and MMR.
3. Observed: wall times of 160s–287s at ~100% CPU, event loop fully blocked. A `sample` profile of the seized process shows a single synchronous microtask dominated by `FindOrderedHashMapEntry` / `FindOrderedHashSetEntry` / `String::SlowEquals` / `StringEqual` — i.e. token-`Set` intersections.

**Root cause**

`mmrRerank` in `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/mmr.ts` pre-tokenizes candidates, but on every selection round it recomputes each remaining candidate's Jaccard similarity against *every* previously selected item — O(rounds × candidates × selected × tokens), effectively cubic in pool size. At 200 candidates this is minutes of synchronous string/Set work with no yield point.

**Fix (PR attached)**

Running-max formulation: each candidate maintains its maximum similarity to the selected set; on each selection round it is compared only against the *newly* selected item. Exact same MMR semantics — ranking output is identical (covered by an explicit ranking-equivalence regression test against a from-scratch reference implementation) — at O(n²).

**Benchmarks (live corpus data, isolated MMR stage)**

| pool | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 40 | 14.7ms | 3.7ms |
| 80 | 104ms | 6.8ms |
| 120 | 347ms | 11.7ms |
| 160 | 903ms | 20.8ms |
| 200 | 1,841ms | 31.7ms (~58×) |

(The 1.8s benchmark figure is the isolated MMR stage; in the live gateway the same stage compounded with other pressure into the multi-minute seizures above.)

**Verification**

- On `release/2026.7.1`: full MMR suite 27/27 including the new ranking-equivalence regression; full build green.
- Adapted to current `main` (test file restructured there): 5/5 including the equivalence regression against main's CJK-aware tokenizer.
- Live: three consecutive broad `corpus=all` searches, including two exact former seizure queries, completed in 6.3–13.4s wall with the fusion stage at 31–773ms. An external CPU watchdog (out-of-process sampler, 2×≥85% trigger) stayed silent throughout — previously it captured the seizure reliably.

**Why this is a liveness bug, not a perf nit**

1. The timeout that guards the search is structurally defeated — in-process timers cannot fire in the loop the search seized.
2. The whole gateway (all channels/heartbeats) dies with it, not just the search.
3. The work is asymptotically avoidable with identical output.

problem_statement:
Photon iMessage: streaming cursor/tofu shows as white square in outbound messages

## Problem
Outbound Photon/iMessage messages could still render a white square/tofu artifact during streaming. In practice it showed up as the streaming cursor/placeholder being displayed inside otherwise normal assistant replies.

This was visible in user-facing iMessage bubbles and was not limited to markdown formatting.

## Root cause
Photon was being treated like a normal streamed platform, so interim updates could include the streaming cursor. On iMessage, that cursor rendered as a visible white box artifact.

## Fix
Make Photon outbound **buffer-only / plain-text-only**:
- suppress the streaming cursor for Photon
- avoid progressive streaming bubbles on Photon
- only deliver the final plain-text message

This also keeps Photon away from rich-text/markdown paths that can leak placeholder characters into the outbound payload.

## Verification
Targeted regression tests passed after the change, including Photon and stream-consumer coverage.

## Notes
This is related to the earlier Photon/iMessage formatting issue, but the concrete bug here is the streaming cursor/tofu artifact.,timeout:60

 macOS/Windows signing and notarization run automatically when the relevant credentials are present in the environment (`CSC_LINK` / `CSC_KEY_PASSWORD` / `APPLE_*` for macOS, `WIN_CSC_*` for Windows).
 
+### macOS permissions and local rebuilds (TCC)
+
+macOS remembers permission grants (Full Disk Access, Desktop/Downloads/Documents,
+Accessibility, Automation, microphone) against the app's *code-signing identity*,
+not its path. Locally built and self-updated apps are signed with a stable
+identifier-pinned ad-hoc signature, so grants persist across updates out of the
+box.
+
+For the strongest guarantee — a certificate-anchored identity, the same
+mechanism yabai/skhd users rely on — create a self-signed code-signing
+certificate once and tell Hermes to use it:
+
+1. Keychain Access → Certificate Assistant → **Create a Certificate…**
+2. Name: `Hermes Local Signing`, Identity Type: *Self-Signed Root*,
+   Certificate Type: **Code Signing**.
+3. `hermes config set desktop.macos_signing_identity "Hermes Local Signing"`
+
+The next update re-signs the rebuilt app with that certificate; every TCC grant
+survives. No Apple Developer account is required. Notarized release builds are
+detected and never re-signed.
+
+One-time note: changing the signing identity (including the first update after
+this fix) changes the app's identity once, so macOS will re-prompt one final
+time. Grants are stable from then on. If a permission gets stuck, reset it with
+`tccutil reset All com.nousresearch.hermes` and re-grant.
+

problem_statement:
feat: sign Hermes.app with Apple Developer ID for stable macOS TCC permissions

### Problem

After every Hermes.app update, all macOS privacy permissions (Accessibility, Screen Recording, Automation, Files & Folders) are revoked. The user must re-grant them manually each time.

**Root cause:** Hermes.app is currently ad-hoc signed (`TeamIdentifier=not set`), so macOS TCC identifies the app solely by its code digest (CDHash), which changes with every binary update.

```
$ codesign -dvvv /Applications/Hermes.app
...
Signature=adhoc
TeamIdentifier=not set
```

macOS version: 26.5.1
Hermes version: 0.15.1

### Proposed solution

Sign the Hermes.app bundle with an **Apple Developer ID Application** certificate and submit it for notarization. This gives the app a stable `TeamIdentifier` that macOS TCC recognizes across updates, so permissions granted once persist forever.

This is standard practice for every major Electron app on macOS (VS Code, Slack, Discord, etc.) — it's a well-established CI/CD step.

### Alternatives considered that do not work

- **Self-signing with a local cert**: macOS does not recognize self-signed Team IDs for TCC purposes.
- **TCC database manipulation**: Blocked by SIP, impractical per-user.
- **Wrapper launcher**: The Hermes process itself makes the TCC-protected calls.
- **Granting to Terminal.app**: Works for CLI but not for the Desktop GUI.

### Additional context

Hundreds of users run Hermes on macOS as a Desktop GUI app. This is the #1 macOS UX friction point — every update forces a trip to System Settings > Privacy & Security to re-enable 3-5 toggles.

problem_statement:
Bug: Windows: `--profile` fails with WinError 32 when Chrome is running (profile copy vs file locks)

### Browser Use Version

0.12.5

### Bug Description, Steps to Reproduce, Screenshots

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 10 / 11 (x64)
- **CLI:** `uvx --from 'browser-use[cli]' browser-use ...`
- **Chrome:** Normal install, `Default` profile, **Chrome already running**

## What happens

```bash
browser-use --headed --profile "Default" open https://example.com
```

Fails with multiple [WinError 32] errors (Chinese locale message: 另一个程序正在使用此文件，进程无法访问。 — The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process.)

Typical locked paths include:

%LocalAppData%\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Network\Cookies
Cookies-journal
Safe Browsing Network\Safe Browsing Cookies
Sessions\Session_*, Tabs_*
The error payload shows a copy from the real Chrome profile into a temp dir such as %TEMP%\browser-use-user-data-dir-*\Default\....

## Why (root cause)
--profile appears to work by copying the Chrome user-data profile into an isolated temp directory, then launching Chromium with that copy.

On Windows, while Chrome is running it holds exclusive locks on many profile files. The copy step then fails with WinError 32.

On macOS/Linux, reading/copying files that another process has open is often still possible; Windows locking is stricter, so this is especially a Windows pain point.

## Impact
Users who expect to reuse an existing Chrome login session via --profile on Windows effectively must fully quit Chrome first, which is easy to miss and hurts the advertised workflow.

## Suggestions
Docs: Explicitly document: on Windows, close Chrome before --profile, or use --connect / --cdp-url with remote debugging enabled.
UX: On WinError 32, detect this pattern and print a short, actionable message (close Chrome or use CDP) instead of a long tuple dump.
Longer term (if feasible): Consider a Windows-friendly approach that avoids copying locked files (e.g. attach via CDP only, or another strategy the team prefers).

## Related
--connect correctly expects a Chrome instance with remote debugging; that path is fine but orthogonal to --profile expectations on Windows.

Thank you for browser-use — happy to help test any fix on Windows.

problem_statement:
Feature Request: `browser-use record` command for session video capture

# Feature Request: `browser-use record` command for session video capture

## Summary

Add `browser-use record start <output.webm>` and `browser-use record stop` CLI commands to capture the current browser session as a video file.

## Motivation

The `browser-use` CLI is great for scripting and automating browser sessions, but there's currently no way to capture a video of what the browser did. Screenshots (`browser-use screenshot`) are useful for spot-checks but lose timing and flow context.

A record command would make browser-use sessions much more useful for:
- **Debugging**: replay exactly what happened in a failed automated run
- **Documentation**: record a user flow walk-through driven by CLI commands
- **Testing**: generate video artifacts from CI to review regressions visually
- **Demos**: automate a product demo and capture it as a video

## Proposed commands

```bash
# Start recording (saves to file when stopped)
browser-use record start /tmp/session.webm

# Stop recording and save the file
browser-use record stop

# One-shot: record while running a command chain
browser-use record start /tmp/session.webm && \
  browser-use open https://example.com && \
  browser-use click 5 && \
  browser-use record stop
```

The session persists via the existing daemon, so recording state could live in the daemon alongside the browser session.

## Implementation path

The underlying `cdp-use` library (also by browser-use) exposes full access to the Chrome DevTools Protocol. CDP has native frame streaming via `Page.startScreencast` / `Page.screencastFrame` / `Page.stopScreencast` — the same mechanism used by Cypress and other tools for headless video recording. This works in headless mode, no screen capture tools required.

See the companion feature request on `cdp-use`: https://github.com/browser-use/cdp-use/issues/19

## Example use case that prompted this request

I'm using `browser-use` CLI as a tool available to AI agents to automate browser interactions — things like walking through a product's first-time user experience and reporting on UX issues. The agent takes screenshots at each step but a continuous video would be far more useful for reviewing the session after the fact, especially for sharing with others.

## Alternatives considered

- **`browser-use screenshot` in a loop**: produces a slideshow, not a real recording; loses timing
- **macOS `screencapture -V`**: only works in `--headed` mode, not headless
- **Playwright `record_video_dir`**: not available since `browser-use` CLI uses `cdp-use`, not Playwright
- **Laminar integration**: great for full observability pipelines, too heavyweight for simple local recording

## Notes

- Should integrate with named sessions (`--session`) so you can record a specific session
- Output format `.webm` is the natural output from CDP screencast frames; `.mp4` conversion could be optional
- Could be gated behind an optional dependency to keep base install lightweight

+        """Parent graph callbacks are loop-bound and must not enter the child loop."""

+        child_callback = object()
+        observed: dict[str, object] = {}
+
+        async def fake_aexecute(task, result_holder=None):
+            effective = ensure_config({"callbacks": [child_callback]})
+            observed["callbacks"] = effective["callbacks"]
+            observed["configurable"] = effective["configurable"]

+        )
+
+        scheduler = concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)
+        token = var_child_runnable_config.set(
+            {
+                "callbacks": [parent_callback, stream_callback],
+                "configurable": {
+                    "thread_id": "parent-thread",
+                    "checkpoint_ns": "parent:task",
+                },
+            }
+        )
+        try:
+            with (
+                patch.object(executor_module, "_scheduler_pool", scheduler),
+                patch.object(executor, "_aexecute", side_effect=fake_aexecute),

problem_statement:
`provide_automatic_options` is weird

While dealing with trying to detect duplicate routes in https://github.com/pallets/werkzeug/issues/3105, I ran into an issue with Flask, which adds `OPTIONS` to every single rule by default.

I started looking into Flask's `provide_automatic_options` feature, and it's just weird.

- Why is there a `PROVIDE_AUTOMATIC_OPTIONS` config? What benefit is there to turning `OPTIONS` off at all, let alone configuring it for a given deployment.
- Flask adds `OPTIONS` to every route, then has a check that runs on dispatching _every_ request to see if the method was `OPTIONS` and `provide_automatic_options` was enabled for the rule. Performing this check for every request seems wasteful, as opposed to adding an actual rule and endpoint so that the routing that's already happening handles it.
    - But adding a rule is also sort of bad, as it results in a bunch of duplicate rules since Flask has no way to know what other rules have already been added. This can be caught with Werkzeug 3.2, and doesn't cause problems in earlier versions, but it's still annoying.
- `provide_automatic_options` can be set as an attribute on the view function. There are some other attributes that are barely documented as well, such as `required_methods`. This is presumably mostly for `View` classes, but works on functions too, making type annotations unhelpful.
- If `PROVIDE_AUTOMATIC_OPTIONS` is disabled (not the default), the logic for the `provide_automatic_options` argument and attribute doesn't work correctly to _enable_ it, it only works for _disabling_.
- The tests for this were incomplete and had some issues. Some other tests were revealed to be adding duplicate rules as well. 

At a minimum I've fixed the enabling issue. I've also got a change that registers a route and view for options instead of using special dispatch logic. We should also consider deprecating the config.

problem_statement:
pass context internally instead of using contextvars

Currently, there are a bunch of different methods on the `Flask` class that run to dispatch each request. Many of these access `request` and other context proxies. We should update them to pass the `AppContext` everywhere instead. This is more convenient after #5812 with only one context object instead of two. As @pgjones pointed out in #5229, not having to access the contextvar is a significant speedup to ASGI Quart, although it doesn't appear to affect WSGI Flask as much. Perhaps if we were serving with greenlets and so contexts were switching more, it would be more noticeable in Flask too.

The obvious problem is that it is a breaking change to the signatures of all these methods. I'm unsure how many methods are affected, but I'm also unsure how many projects are even subclassing `Flask` to override any of the methods. The fact that the methods are public seems unintentional, compared to the much more common ways of configuring and customizing an app.

We could continue to support both signatures, showing a deprecation warning for the old one, by adding some detection to `Flask.__init__`. This would add some amount of time during app setup, but wouldn't affect runtime performance of the app.

---

Another idea I had for the future was to have `@route` and other decorators inspect the signature of the decorated function, to allow injecting `request`, `app`, etc. if users would rather use that pattern than import the proxies. Having the request object directly available in all the dispatch methods would make this more straightforward. User code would be able to choose what pattern they want, the current proxy pattern would never be deprecated for user code.

problem_statement: API: setitem-with-expansion casting This is a doozy: I'm working through the issues with the setitem-with-expansion tag and about half of them are of the form "i added a row and got unwanted casting." Most of those are int->float, some are EA->object. At least one is object->non_object (when the original is empty we special-case). Some of these (`df.loc[new_row] = values`) go through a path that uses concat. Others (`df.loc[new_row, :] = values` go through a path that reindexes instead. These two paths can give subtly different behaviors: ``` df = pd.DataFrame({"A": [1, 2], "B": [3, 4]}) df2 = df.copy() df.loc[2] = 5 df2.loc[2, :] = 5 assert (df.dtypes == "int64").all() assert (df2.dtypes == "float64").all() ``` I have a branch that updates the concat-codepath to call _cast_pointwise_result on the new values to try to cast to the column's original dtype, but there are some problems there: 1) Doing that without patching the reindex path introduces even more inconsistencies 2) We have exactly one test case (test_partial_setting) that seems to be expecting non-casting: ``` ser = pd.Series([1, 2, 3]) ser.loc[5] = 5.0 expected = Series([1, 2, 3, 5.0], index=[0, 1, 2, 5], dtype="float64") tm.assert_series_equal(ser, expected) ``` 3) The elegant solution of using cast_pointwise_result requires adding to NumpyEA._cast_pointwise_result and MaskedEA._cast_pointwise_result checks for "if the original is integer and the result is all-round floats, cast back to ints". This change affects a bunch of map/apply/combine behavior that may not be desired. Of course we could put those checks outside the _cast_pointwise_result calls, they just become much less elegant. In the background there is also the consideration that I'm hoping that in 4.0 we will get to nullable-by-default, in which case the reindex codepath will not do any casting, so the issue will fix itself for those cases. Plausibly we could refactor to always go down that path and get consistency that way. ATM I'm inclined to say that the test referenced in point 2) is wrong/undesired, and the setitem-with-expansion cases should behave like the non-expansion cases as much as possible (i.e. it will cast round floats to ints). I'm taking a look at what it would take to patch the reindexing codepath with the same _cast_pointwise_result logic as the concat codepath, but i think its a bit more involved. Assuming that isn't feasible, should we try to fix the concat codepaths alone? Update Two more differences in the reindex path are that a) we get the PDEP-6 disallowing of extra casting behavior and b) we don't get the special-casing of empty cases.

### Description

---

**Title:** Nested subgraph with own checkpointer has writes stored under wrong namespace (regression in 1.2.3)

---

**Describe the bug**

When a compiled child graph (with its own fixed `thread_id`) is invoked from within a parent graph node, its checkpoint state becomes unreadable on subsequent turns. The writes reach the checkpointer storage under the correct `thread_id` key, but `get_state` returns `None` — indicating the data is stored under a `checkpoint_ns` inherited from the parent's run context, making it unreachable when the child reads back with its own config.

On the next turn the child loads a blank state and re-runs from scratch, losing all progress.

This was introduced in 1.2.3 and is still present in 1.2.4. Last good version is 1.2.2.

**To Reproduce**

```python
import asyncio
from typing import TypedDict
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver

CHILD_THREAD_ID = "child-fixed-thread"

def build_child(checkpointer):
    class ChildState(TypedDict):
        count: int

    def child_node(state):
        count = state.get("count") or 0
        return {"count": count + 1}

    g = StateGraph(ChildState)
    g.add_node("n", child_node)
    g.set_entry_point("n")
    g.add_edge("n", END)
    return g.compile(checkpointer=checkpointer)

def build_parent(child_compiled, checkpointer):
    class ParentState(TypedDict):
        turn: int

    async def parent_node(state):
        turn = state.get("turn") or 0
        child_input = {"count": 0} if turn == 0 else {}
        await child_compiled.ainvoke(
            child_input,
            config={"configurable": {"thread_id": CHILD_THREAD_ID}},
        )
        return {"turn": turn + 1}

    g = StateGraph(ParentState)
    g.add_node("p", parent_node)
    g.set_entry_point("p")
    g.add_edge("p", END)
    return g.compile(checkpointer=checkpointer)

async def main():
    # Single shared checkpointer — parent and child use the same instance,
    # differentiated only by thread_id. This matches the common pattern of
    # a top-level graph delegating to persistent sub-workflows.
    shared_cp = MemorySaver()
    child_compiled = build_child(shared_cp)
    parent_compiled = build_parent(child_compiled, shared_cp)

    parent_config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "parent-thread"}}
    child_config  = {"configurable": {"thread_id": CHILD_THREAD_ID}}

    # Turn 1
    await parent_compiled.ainvoke({"turn": 0}, config=parent_config)
    s1 = child_compiled.get_state(child_config)
    print(f"Storage keys after turn 1: {list(shared_cp.storage.keys())}")
    print(f"Child count after turn 1:  {s1.values.get('count') if s1 and s1.values else None}")

    # Turn 2
    await parent_compiled.ainvoke({}, config=parent_config)
    s2 = child_compiled.get_state(child_config)
    count = s2.values.get("count") if s2 and s2.values else None
    print(f"Child count after turn 2:  {count}")
    print("PASS" if count == 2 else "FAIL")

asyncio.run(main())
```

**Expected behavior**

```
Storage keys after turn 1: ['parent-thread', 'child-fixed-thread']
Child count after turn 1:  1
Child count after turn 2:  2   ← child resumed from checkpoint
PASS
```

**Actual behavior (1.2.3 / 1.2.4)**

```
Storage keys after turn 1: ['parent-thread', 'child-fixed-thread']
Child count after turn 1:  None   ← written but unreadable
Child count after turn 2:  None   ← child re-ran from scratch
FAIL
```

Note: `child-fixed-thread` *does* appear in storage, so the write is reaching the checkpointer. But `get_state` returns `None`, indicating the checkpoint was stored under a `checkpoint_ns` inherited from the parent's run context rather than the child's own namespace. On the next turn the child reads back an empty state.

**Version bisect**

| Version | Result    |
| ------- | --------- |
| 1.2.2   | ✅ works  |
| 1.2.3   | ❌ broken |
| 1.2.4   | ❌ broken |

Standalone invocation (same child graph called directly, not inside a parent node) works correctly in all versions.

**Root cause hypothesis**

The `ensure_config` change in 1.2.3 ("merge instead of overwrite for callbacks, tags, metadata, configurable") causes the child graph to inherit the parent's `checkpoint_ns` when invoked from within a parent node. The child's writes are stored under that inherited namespace, so `get_state` called with the child's own config finds nothing.

**Environment**

- `langgraph`: 1.2.4
- `langgraph-checkpoint`: 4.1.1
- Python: 3.12

BUG: Data race reading and writing np.random.seed

### Describe the issue:

This is not terribly surprising, but the attached example is a TSAN data race under NumPy 2.5.1.

While you can certainly say "you shouldn't be setting the seed concurrently from multiple threads", doing so shouldn't be a C-level race because that is UB.

```python
import threading
import time

from absl.testing import absltest
import numpy as np


class TsanFailureTest(absltest.TestCase):

  def test_mt19937_seed_get_state_race(self):
    stop = False

    def seeder():
      while not stop:
        np.random.seed(12345)

    def getter():
      while not stop:
        _ = np.random.get_state()

    threads = [
        threading.Thread(target=seeder) for _ in range(4)
    ] + [
        threading.Thread(target=getter) for _ in range(4)
    ]

    for t in threads:
      t.start()

    time.sleep(0.5)
    stop = True

    for t in threads:
      t.join()


if __name__ == "__main__":
  absltest.main()

problem_statement:
Windows bash detection fails when git comes from a native MSYS2 environment (ucrt64/clang64/clangarm64)

### What version of Kimi Code is running?

0.23.5

### Which open platform/subscription were you using?

Kimi Code

### Which model were you using?

kimi-for-coding

### What platform is your computer?

_No response_

### What issue are you seeing?

On Windows, starting kimi-code fails with:

Git Bash was not found on this Windows host. Install Git for Windows
from https://gitforwindows.org/ or set KIMI_SHELL_PATH to a bash.exe.
Checked: ...

This happens on hosts where git comes from a native MSYS2 mingw-w64
package instead of msys's git, even though bash exists at
`C:\msys64\usr\bin\bash.exe`.

Root cause: the shell probe infers the install root from
`git --exec-path` by scanning the path for known prefix segments, but
**only `mingw32`/`mingw64` are recognised** — the prefixes Git for Windows
still uses, but which MSYS2 upstream has deprecated. **Modern MSYS2
toolchains live under `ucrt64` (the default `MSYSTEM`), `clang64`, and
`clangarm64`**, so a native git's exec path matches nothing and the root
cannot be inferred. Setting `KIMI_SHELL_PATH` works around it, but
auto-detection fails before any session starts, so session id and
context usage don't apply.


### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Windows host with MSYS2 installed at the default `C:\msys64`.
2. `pacman -S mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-git`, and put
   `C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin` on PATH (do NOT install Git for Windows).
3. `git --exec-path` prints `C:/msys64/ucrt64/libexec/git-core`.
4. Launch kimi-code.

### What is the expected behavior?

Expected: detection resolves `C:\msys64\usr\bin\bash.exe` from the
git exec path. Actual: `KaosShellNotFoundError` as above.

### Additional information

_No response_

@@ -0,0 +1,198 @@
+package ai.openclaw.app.ui
+
+import ai.openclaw.app.ui.design.ClawDesignTheme
+import ai.openclaw.app.ui.design.MascotMood
+import android.content.Context
+import android.provider.Settings
+import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Box
+import androidx.compose.foundation.layout.size
+import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
+import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
+import androidx.compose.ui.draw.clipToBounds
+import androidx.compose.ui.platform.testTag
+import androidx.compose.ui.test.DeviceConfigurationOverride
+import androidx.compose.ui.test.FontScale
+import androidx.compose.ui.test.assertIsDisplayed
+import androidx.compose.ui.test.getUnclippedBoundsInRoot
+import androidx.compose.ui.test.hasScrollAction
+import androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.v2.createComposeRule
+import androidx.compose.ui.test.onNodeWithTag
+import androidx.compose.ui.test.onNodeWithText
+import androidx.compose.ui.test.performClick
+import androidx.compose.ui.test.performScrollTo
+import androidx.compose.ui.test.performTouchInput
+import androidx.compose.ui.test.swipeUp
+import androidx.compose.ui.unit.Dp
+import androidx.compose.ui.unit.DpRect
+import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
+import androidx.test.core.app.ApplicationProvider
+import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
+import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
+import org.junit.Before
+import org.junit.Rule
+import org.junit.Test
+import org.junit.runner.RunWith
+import org.robolectric.RobolectricTestRunner
+import org.robolectric.annotation.Config
+
+private const val OnboardingViewportTag = "initial-onboarding-viewport"
+
+@RunWith(RobolectricTestRunner::class)
+@Config(qualifiers = "w360dp-h720dp-420dpi")
+class InitialOnboardingLayoutTest {
+  @get:Rule
+  val composeRule = createComposeRule()
+
+  @Before
+  fun disableMascotAnimations() {
+    val context = ApplicationProvider.getApplicationContext<Context>()
+    Settings.Global.putFloat(context.contentResolver, Settings.Global.ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE, 0f)
+  }
+
+  @Test
+  fun defaultFontKeepsWelcomeContentAndActionVisible() {
+    var connectClicked = false
+    setContent(fontScale = 1f, viewportHeight = 720.dp) {
+      WelcomeScreen(mascotMood = MascotMood.Idle, onConnect = { connectClicked = true })
+    }
+
+    composeRule.onNodeWithText("Security notice").assertIsDisplayed()
+    composeRule.onNodeWithText("Continue").assertIsDisplayed().performClick()
+    assertTrue(connectClicked)
+  }
+
+  @Test
+  fun largeFontKeepsWelcomeActionFixedWhileContentScrolls() {
+    var connectClicked = false
+    setContent(fontScale = 1.3f, viewportHeight = 480.dp) {
+      WelcomeScreen(mascotMood = MascotMood.Idle, onConnect = { connectClicked = true })
+    }
+
+    val viewport = composeRule.onNodeWithTag(OnboardingViewportTag)
+    val content = composeRule.onNodeWithText("Security notice")
+    val action = composeRule.onNodeWithText("Continue").assertIsDisplayed()
+    val scrollable = composeRule.onNode(hasScrollAction()).assertExists()
+    val viewportBounds = viewport.getUnclippedBoundsInRoot()
+    val contentBeforeScroll = content.getUnclippedBoundsInRoot()
+    val actionBeforeScroll = action.getUnclippedBoundsInRoot()
+    assertFullyInside(actionBeforeScroll, viewportBounds, "Welcome action")
+
+    scrollable.performTouchInput { swipeUp() }
+    composeRule.waitForIdle()
+
+    val contentAfterScroll = content.getUnclippedBoundsInRoot()
+    val actionAfterScroll = action.getUnclippedBoundsInRoot()
+    assertTrue("Welcome content should move upward after a swipe", contentAfterScroll.top < contentBeforeScroll.top)
+    assertEquals("Welcome action should remain fixed while content scrolls", actionBeforeScroll, actionAfterScroll)
+    assertFullyInside(actionAfterScroll, viewportBounds, "Welcome action")
+
+    content.performScrollTo().assertIsDisplayed()
+    composeRule.waitForIdle()
+
+    val actionAfterContentReached = action.getUnclippedBoundsInRoot()
+    assertEquals("Welcome action should remain fixed when content is reached", actionBeforeScroll, actionAfterContentReached)
+    assertFullyInside(actionAfterContentReached, viewportBounds, "Welcome action")
+    action.assertIsDisplayed().performClick()
+    assertTrue(connectClicked)
+  }
+
+  @Test
+  fun defaultFontKeepsGatewayContentAndActionsVisible() {
+    var manualSetupClicked = false
+    setContent(fontScale = 1f, viewportHeight = 720.dp) {
+      GatewaySetupScreen(
+        nearbyGateway = null,
+        onBack = {},
+        onSetupCode = {},
+        onManualSetup = { manualSetupClicked = true },
+      )
+    }
+
+    composeRule.onNodeWithText("Android setup guide").assertIsDisplayed()
+    composeRule.onNodeWithText("Scan QR or setup code").assertIsDisplayed()
+    composeRule.onNodeWithText("Set up manually").assertIsDisplayed().performClick()
+    assertTrue(manualSetupClicked)
+  }
+
+  @Test
+  fun largeFontKeepsGatewayActionsFixedWhileContentScrolls() {
+    var setupCodeClicked = false
+    setContent(fontScale = 1.3f, viewportHeight = 480.dp) {
+      GatewaySetupScreen(
+        nearbyGateway = null,
+        onBack = {},
+        onSetupCode = { setupCodeClicked = true },
+        onManualSetup = {},
+      )
+    }
+
+    val viewport = composeRule.onNodeWithTag(OnboardingViewportTag)
+    val content = composeRule.onNodeWithText("Android setup guide")
+    val primaryAction = composeRule.onNodeWithText("Scan QR or setup code").assertIsDisplayed()
+    val secondaryAction = composeRule.onNodeWithText("Set up manually").assertIsDisplayed()
+    val scrollable = composeRule.onNode(hasScrollAction()).assertExists()
+    val viewportBounds = viewport.getUnclippedBoundsInRoot()
+    val contentBeforeScroll = content.getUnclippedBoundsInRoot()
+    val primaryActionBeforeScroll = primaryAction.getUnclippedBoundsInRoot()
+    val secondaryActionBeforeScroll = secondaryAction.getUnclippedBoundsInRoot()
+    assertFullyInside(primaryActionBeforeScroll, viewportBounds, "Gateway primary action")
+    assertFullyInside(secondaryActionBeforeScroll, viewportBounds, "Gateway secondary action")
+
+    scrollable.performTouchInput { swipeUp() }
+    composeRule.waitForIdle()
+
+    val contentAfterScroll = content.getUnclippedBoundsInRoot()
+    val primaryActionAfterScroll = primaryAction.getUnclippedBoundsInRoot()
+    val secondaryActionAfterScroll = secondaryAction.getUnclippedBoundsInRoot()
+    assertTrue("Gateway content should move upward after a swipe", contentAfterScroll.top < contentBeforeScroll.top)
+    assertEquals("Gateway primary action should remain fixed while content scrolls", primaryActionBeforeScroll, primaryActionAfterScroll)
+    assertEquals("Gateway secondary action should remain fixed while content scrolls", secondaryActionBeforeScroll, secondaryActionAfterScroll)
+    assertFullyInside(primaryActionAfterScroll, viewportBounds, "Gateway primary action")
+    assertFullyInside(secondaryActionAfterScroll, viewportBounds, "Gateway secondary action")
+
+    content.performScrollTo().assertIsDisplayed()
+    composeRule.waitForIdle()
+
+    val primaryActionAfterContentReached = primaryAction.getUnclippedBoundsInRoot()
+    val secondaryActionAfterContentReached = secondaryAction.getUnclippedBoundsInRoot()
+    assertEquals("Gateway primary action should remain fixed when content is reached", primaryActionBeforeScroll, primaryActionAfterContentReached)
+    assertEquals("Gateway secondary action should remain fixed when content is reached", secondaryActionBeforeScroll, secondaryActionAfterContentReached)
+    assertFullyInside(primaryActionAfterContentReached, viewportBounds, "Gateway primary action")
+    assertFullyInside(secondaryActionAfterContentReached, viewportBounds, "Gateway secondary action")
+    primaryAction.assertIsDisplayed().performClick()
+    assertTrue(setupCodeClicked)
+  }
+
+  private fun setContent(
+    fontScale: Float,
+    viewportHeight: Dp,
+    content: @Composable () -> Unit,
+  ) {
+    composeRule.setContent {
+      DeviceConfigurationOverride(DeviceConfigurationOverride.FontScale(fontScale)) {
+        ClawDesignTheme {
+          Box(
+            modifier =
+              Modifier
+                .size(width = 360.dp, height = viewportHeight)
+                .clipToBounds()
+                .testTag(OnboardingViewportTag),
+          ) {
+            content()
+          }
+        }
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  private fun assertFullyInside(
+    child: DpRect,
+    parent: DpRect,
+    label: String,
+  ) {
+    assertTrue("$label should stay inside the viewport's left edge", child.left >= parent.left)
+    assertTrue("$label should stay inside the viewport's top edge", child.top >= parent.top)
+    assertTrue("$label should stay inside the viewport's right edge", child.right <= parent.right)
+    assertTrue("$label should stay inside the viewport's bottom edge", child.bottom <= parent.bottom)
+  }
+}
problem_statement: [Bug]: android welcome screen not scrollable at large font size = can't tap continue to begin setup ### Bug type Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash) ### Beta release blocker No ### Summary On Android, using larger system Font sizes leads first-run OpenClaw welcome screen to overflow vertically, the **Continue** button is pushed below the bottom of the screen, and as screen cannot be scrolled, you can't tap continue to begin setup. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Install OpenClaw fresh, or clear its app storage so the welcome screen appears. 2. In Android, open **Settings → Display → Display size and text**. 3. Set **Font size** to **Large**. 4. Open OpenClaw. 5. On the welcome screen, try to reach the Continue button below the security note. ### Expected behavior The welcome screen should remain usable at Android’s supported larger font sizes: - The content should scroll vertically when it exceeds the viewport; and/or - The Continue action should remain reachable/anchored within the viewport. ### Actual behavior The welcome content extends beyond the bottom of the display. The Continue button cannot be reached, and the welcome screen does not scroll. Lowering the Android system Font size makes the button visible again, which allows setup to continue. ### OpenClaw version v2026.7.1 ### Operating system Android v13, Android v16 ### Install method Play store ### Model n/a ### Provider / routing chain n/a ### Additional provider/model setup details _No response_ ### Logs ```shell ``` ### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence ### Impact and severity Affected: Certain Android 13 & Android 16 new users, Likely all Android new users with large text sizes Severity: Prevents app setup & usage unless text size reduced to small Frequency: Always on App initialization welcome screen Consequence: Can't use app ### Additional information Tested on hardware Device/OS: Samsung Galaxy A16 5G sm-a166p, Android 16. Tested on software Pixel emulator: Host: Win11 Android Studio: Quail 2 (2026.1.2) Virtual device: Pixel 6a, portrait, 1080 × 2400, System image: Android 13 / API 33, Google Play. Android OpenClaw: official Play Store app, version v2026.7.1

problem_statement:
iOS native Talk/Wake TTS ignores configured Speech Language — Turkish read with en-US voice (AVSpeechSynthesizer locale not set)

## Summary

On the official iOS app with the **native system-voice fallback active** (Active Voice: "iOS Speech + TTS"), assistant replies are spoken with the device-default **en-US** voice regardless of the configured **Speech Language**. Turkish replies are read using English grapheme-to-phoneme rules — "English-accented Turkish" — which makes non-English Talk output sound wrong/unintelligible.

The native fallback itself works (this build already speaks without ElevenLabs credentials, i.e. the ask in #113056 is present here). The remaining bug is that the fallback **ignores the configured Speech Language locale** for TTS output.

## Environment

- OpenClaw Gateway: 2026.7.1-2
- iOS app: official build
- Provider: **Gateway Default**
- Voice Mode: **ElevenLabs**
- Active Voice: **iOS Speech + TTS** (native fallback)
- Transport: **Native**
- Speech Language: **Türkçe (Türkiye)**
- API Key: **Not configured**

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use iOS Talk with no ElevenLabs/OpenAI key configured → the native "iOS Speech + TTS" fallback is active.
2. Set **Speech Language** to **Türkçe (Türkiye)**.
3. Have the assistant reply in Turkish.
4. Listen: the Turkish text is spoken with an English voice/pronunciation.

## Expected behavior

The native TTS path should set `AVSpeechUtterance.voice` to an `AVSpeechSynthesisVoice` matching the configured **Speech Language** (e.g. `tr-TR`, such as Yelda) — or run language detection on the reply text — so Turkish is read with a Turkish voice.

## Actual behavior

- `AVSpeechUtterance` language defaults to `en-US` (app/device default).
- The **Speech Language: Türkçe** setting is applied only to speech **recognition (STT)**, not to the TTS utterance.
- iOS system **Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content → Default Language / Detect Languages** does **not** affect third-party `AVSpeechSynthesizer` output, so there is no user-side workaround from iOS Settings (verified: setting Default Language = Turkish and downloading the Turkish "Yelda" voice does not change app output).

## Notes

- The server-side Talk voice directive `lang` key (e.g. `{ "lang": "tr-TR" }`) is **not honored** on the native path — sending it produced no change.
- Related: #113056 (native system-voice fallback for Talk/Wake).

## Suggested fix

Reuse the configured Speech Language locale (or language-detect the reply text) to select the `AVSpeechSynthesisVoice`, defaulting to a matching installed voice and falling back gracefully if none is installed. ElevenLabs/OpenAI Realtime remain opt-in upgrades.

problem_statement:
[Bug]: Sanitized MCP tool names can collide and silently replace valid tools

## Summary

Hermes normalizes MCP server and tool name components by replacing non-alphanumeric characters with `_`. Distinct valid raw names can therefore collapse to the same registry name.

Examples:

- `read-file`, `read_file`, and `read.file` on server `files` all become `mcp__files__read_file`
- servers `foo-bar` and `foo_bar`, each exposing `search`, both become `mcp__foo_bar__search`

The current registration path permits MCP-to-MCP replacement, so one valid tool can silently overwrite another depending on registration order.

## Impact

This can cause:

- tool calls to execute the wrong MCP handler
- valid tools to disappear or be replaced without an actionable error
- dynamic refreshes to retain or rewrite the wrong normalized entry
- raw tool names to collide with generated MCP utility tools such as `list_resources`
- parallel-safety and tool-provenance tracking to conflate distinct raw server names

This is especially difficult to diagnose because the exposed normalized name still looks valid.

## Expected behavior

Ambiguous normalized names should never silently select a winner.

A safe behavior would be:

- reject cross-toolset shadowing atomically and preserve the existing owner
- detect same-server collisions before registration and skip every ambiguous candidate in that group
- log the raw origins that collapsed to the same registry name
- preserve all non-conflicting tools
- remove a previously registered tool if a dynamic refresh makes its normalized name ambiguous
- track parallel-safety and provenance using exact raw server identities

## Reproduction outline

1. Configure an MCP server that exposes both `read-file` and `read_file`.
2. Start Hermes and inspect the registered tool names.
3. Both raw names normalize to `mcp__<server>__read_file`, so only one handler can occupy that registry entry.

A similar collision occurs across two configured servers named `foo-bar` and `foo_bar`.

## Proposed regression coverage

- same-server normalization collision
- cross-server normalization collision
- raw tool collision with generated resource/prompt utilities
- dynamic refresh from a unique name to an ambiguous pair
- concurrent cross-toolset registration race
- exact raw server identity for parallel-safety and provenance

I have a local fix and regression tests prepared, and I’d like to work on this issue myself.

problem_statement:
[Bug]: Native Gemini mismatches bridged functionCall/functionResponse names after Tool Search execution

## Summary

When native Gemini executes an MCP or plugin tool through the tiered Tool Search `tool_call` bridge, Hermes can send different names for the matching Gemini `functionCall` and `functionResponse` parts.

The assistant turn is serialized with:

```json
{"functionCall": {"name": "tool_call", "id": "call_1", "args": {"name": "mcp__github__create_issue", "arguments": {}}}}
```

After the bridge unwraps and executes the underlying tool, the result message carries the internal tool name. The native Gemini adapter currently prefers that result name, producing:

```json
{"functionResponse": {"name": "mcp__github__create_issue", "id": "call_1", "response": {}}}
```

Gemini requires the response name to match the corresponding call name, so the next provider turn can fail with an invalid request after the underlying tool has already executed.

## Reproduction

1. Use the native Gemini provider with tiered tool disclosure enabled.
2. Expose an MCP or plugin tool, which is deferred behind `tool_call`.
3. Let the model call `tool_call` with an underlying tool such as `mcp__github__create_issue`.
4. Execute the tool and build the next native Gemini request from the transcript.
5. Inspect the generated contents.

The `functionCall.name` is `tool_call`, while the matching `functionResponse.name` is the unwrapped MCP/plugin tool name.

## Root cause

`_build_gemini_contents()` records the original wire-visible call name by `tool_call_id`, but `_translate_tool_result_to_gemini()` currently resolves the response name in this order:

```python
message.get("name")
or tool_name_by_call_id.get(tool_call_id)
```

The executor intentionally stores the unwrapped internal tool name on the result message for dispatch, hooks, logging, and guardrails. That internal name therefore overrides the call-ID mapping that represents the actual Gemini `functionCall.name`.

## Expected behavior

For a result associated with a known call ID, `functionResponse.name` should echo the original wire-visible `functionCall.name`. The internal unwrapped tool name should remain available on the Hermes transcript for execution metadata.

## Impact

This affects native Gemini turns that execute deferred MCP/plugin tools through the default Tool Search bridge. A provider rejection can occur only after the real tool has completed, so retrying the user action can duplicate side effects such as creating issues, sending messages, or mutating external systems.

## Proposed fix

Prefer `tool_name_by_call_id[tool_call_id]` over the result message's internal `name` when translating a native Gemini function response, with the existing result name retained as the fallback for transcripts that do not include a matching assistant call.

Add a regression test that builds a transcript containing a `tool_call` assistant call and an MCP-named tool result, then asserts that both Gemini parts use `tool_call`.

problem_statement:
fix(tools): schema sanitizer corrupts dependentRequired on MCP tools (HTTP 400)

## Summary

After enabling GitHub Copilot MCP, Hermes conversations immediately fail with HTTP 400 schema validation errors. Providers reject the tool list because `mcp__github__search_issues` carries a corrupted `dependentRequired` field: property-name **strings** are rewritten into empty object schemas.

Confirmed on **xAI (xai-oauth)**, **OpenAI API**, and **openai-codex**. One bad tool schema aborts the entire turn (non-retryable client error).

## Environment

- Hermes: **v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2)** · upstream `7e84d2b5`
- Install: git (`~/.hermes/hermes-agent`)
- Host: WSL2 Ubuntu on Windows
- MCP server: `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/`
- Culprit tool: `mcp__github__search_issues`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure GitHub Copilot MCP:

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  github:
    transport: http
    url: https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/
    headers:
      Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

2. Start Hermes TUI/CLI (any session that loads MCP tools).
3. Send any message with xAI, OpenAI, or Codex as the active provider.
4. Observe non-retryable HTTP 400; no useful model reply.

### Minimal sanitizer repro

```bash
cd ~/.hermes/hermes-agent
./venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
from tools.schema_sanitizer import _sanitize_node
import json
schema = {
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "owner": {"type": "string"},
    "repo": {"type": "string"},
  },
  "dependentRequired": {
    "owner": ["repo"],
    "repo": ["owner"],
  },
}
print(json.dumps(_sanitize_node(schema, path="test").get("dependentRequired"), indent=2))
PY
```

**Actual (broken):**

```json
{
  "owner": [{"type": "object", "properties": {}}],
  "repo": [{"type": "object", "properties": {}}]
}
```

**Expected:**

```json
{
  "owner": ["repo"],
  "repo": ["owner"]
}
```

## Expected vs Actual

| | |
|--|--|
| **Expected** | Valid JSON Schema `dependentRequired` maps (`dict[str, list[str]]`) are preserved when MCP tools are sanitized and sent to providers. |
| **Actual** | `_sanitize_node` recurses into `dependentRequired` value lists, treats property-name strings as bare schemas, and rewrites them to `{"type":"object","properties":{}}`. Providers reject the request with HTTP 400. |

## Evidence

### xAI

```text
HTTP 400: {"code":"invalid-argument","error":"Invalid request content: Schema validation failed:
[standard_violation] /dependentRequired/owner/0: {\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{}} is not of type \"string\";
[standard_violation] /dependentRequired/repo/0: {\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{}} is not of type \"string\""}
```

### OpenAI / Codex

```text
HTTP 400: Invalid schema for function 'mcp__github__search_issues':
{'type': 'object', 'properties': {}} is not of type 'string'.
param: tools[N].parameters  code: invalid_function_parameters
```

### Request dump

From `~/.hermes/sessions/request_dump_*.json`, the tool parameters for `mcp__github__search_issues` include:

```json
"dependentRequired": {
  "owner": [{"type": "object", "properties": {}}],
  "repo": [{"type": "object", "properties": {}}]
}
```

Agent log:

```text
MCP server 'github' (HTTP): registered 51 tool(s): ... mcp__github__search_issues ...
API call failed ... Non-retryable client error: Error code: 400 ...
```

## Root Cause

File: `tools/schema_sanitizer.py` → `_sanitize_node`

The pass-through set for non-schema sibling keywords includes `required`, `enum`, and `examples`, but **not** `dependentRequired`.

The same function already documents this failure mode for `required`:

> Recursing into these with `_sanitize_node()` would mis-interpret literal strings like `"path"` as bare-string schemas and replace them with `{"type": "object"}` dicts.

`sanitize_tool_schemas()` is invoked from `model_tools.py` for the full tool list (including MCP-derived tools), so any MCP tool that ships `dependentRequired` is corrupted before the API call.

Trigger observed: GitHub Copilot MCP tool `search_issues`. Any other MCP tool using `dependentRequired` would hit the same path.

## Suggested Fix

1. In `_sanitize_node`, treat `dependentRequired` like `required` (deep-copy / pass-through; do **not** recurse list items as schemas). Values must remain `dict[str, list[str]]`.
2. Add a regression test in `tests/tools/test_schema_sanitizer.py` covering a GitHub-MCP-shaped `dependentRequired` fixture.

## Workaround

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  github:
    enabled: false
```

Then start a new session / restart gateway. Chat works without GitHub MCP. Re-enabling without a sanitizer fix restores the 400.

## Impact

- **High:** With GitHub MCP enabled, every model turn can fail with a non-retryable 400 before any assistant text is produced.
- Disabling GitHub MCP restores chat but removes those tools.
- Not limited to one provider; switching models does not help while the bad tool remains registered.

    capture failed: cua-driver list_windows failed: session '<session-id>' has ended; tool call 'list_windows' was rejected. Call start_session with this id to revive it before issuing further actions, or use a new session id.

    This error occurs reliably and prevents any form of UI interaction via computer_use.

    Steps to Reproduce
    1.  Launch Hermes Agent on the specified Windows 11 environment.
    2.  Ensure cua-driver is upgraded to 0.12.6 and no zombie processes are active (as detailed in "What we ruled out" below).
    3.  Launch any desktop application (e.g., start notepad.exe, start calc.exe) via terminal tool.
    4.  Attempt computer_use(action='capture', mode='som', app='screen') or
    computer_use(action='capture', mode='vision', app='screen').

    Expected Behavior
    capture() should succeed, return a screenshot and/or accessibility tree data, and the cua-driver session should remain active for subsequent interactions.

    Actual Behavior
    The capture() call fails immediately with the "session has ended" error, indicating a cua-driver session crash or premature termination. A new session ID is generated on the next computer_use call, but that new session also dies immediately upon the next capture() attempt.

    What We Ruled Out / Troubleshooting Performed
    - Zombie elevated cua-driver processes: Initially, an elevated cua-driver process (PID 28024) was found blocking. This was manually killed by the user via Task Manager (as Administrator). Subsequent tasklist | findstr cua-driver confirmed a clean state before further tests.
    - Outdated driver version: cua-driver was successfully upgraded from 0.8.3 to 0.12.6 using hermes computer-use install --upgrade. hermes computer_use doctor consistently reported cua-driver 0.12.6 as active and healthy after the upgrade and process cleanup.
    - computer_use parameter usage: Tried both mode='som' and mode='vision', and with/without app='screen' (or specific app names). The failure pattern remains consistent.
    - Session isolation / Session 0: Verified that Hermes Agent and the interactive desktop
    shell (explorer.exe) are running in the same interactive user session. This was confirmed
    using two separate commands: powershell -Command '(Get-Process -Id $PID).SessionId' for the
    Hermes process itself, and `powershell -Command '(Get-Process -Name explorer | Select-Object
    -First 1).SessionId' for the interactive desktop shell. Both commands returned SessionId 3`.
    - Target app not existing: Confirmed applications like Calculator (calc.exe) are present
    and launch correctly (verified via start calc.exe returning exit code 0). The issue is not the
    target app's existence, but cua-driver's inability to capture its window.
    - VM/RDP graphics capture limitations: User explicitly confirmed the environment is a physical PC with direct keyboard and monitor access, ruling out known Windows Graphics Capture API compatibility issues with virtual/remote desktops.
    - hermes computer_use doctor status: Immediately prior to every failed capture attempt, hermes computer_use doctor consistently reports all checks as ✅ ok, including ax_capability and screen_capture_capability. This indicates a significant discrepancy between diagnostic reporting and actual operational stability.

    Conclusion
    Despite cua-driver being up-to-date, all diagnostics passing, and running in a standard
    interactive desktop session on a physical PC, the cua-driver session consistently terminates
    when computer_use(action='capture') is called. This indicates a severe stability issue or a
    bug within cua-driver itself when running on the specified Windows 11 environment, preventing Hermes Agent from performing any reliable desktop UI automation.

problem_statement:
Profile routing: route secret does not authorize the profile; /p/{profile} prefix now mirrored onto the API server

### Summary

`/p/<profile>/webhooks/<route>` addresses a named profile, but the route secret does not authorize *which* profile a request may execute as. A single valid secret can trigger execution under any configured profile.

Filing as a regular issue, not through the security channel: SECURITY.md §2.2 states Hermes Agent is "a single-tenant personal agent" and does not name profile isolation as a boundary, so per §3.2 this is a functional gap rather than a vulnerability. Flagging it because the v2026.7.20 profile-routing work makes profiles look like an isolation mechanism to operators, and the docs invite that reading.

### What the release notes suggest

> *"A single multiplexed gateway sharing one bot token can now route specific guilds, channels, or threads to different profiles — each with **fully isolated config, skills, memory, and secrets**."*

An operator reading "fully isolated … secrets" will reasonably conclude that a webhook addressed to profile `A` cannot act as profile `B`. On v0.19.0 that does not hold.

### Observed

A webhook request bearing a valid route secret, addressed to one profile's path prefix, returns `HTTP 202` and executes — with no check binding the secret to the profile named in the path.

Two related observations from the same investigation:

1. **The `/p/{profile}` prefix is now mirrored onto the API server**, so the same unbound-secret pattern exists on a second surface as of this release.
2. **Secret scoping is partial.** Roughly 32 call sites read credentials through the profile-scoped accessor, against ~167 raw `os.getenv` reads. So "isolated secrets" holds for the scoped paths and not for the rest.

### Why it matters operationally

The natural use of profile routing is one agent per context — for us, a `foreman` profile working an internal repo and a separate profile working a client's. If a single secret can execute as either, profiles provide organisational separation but not containment, and an operator who reads the release note as containment will over-trust the arrangement.

### Suggested resolutions, in ascending order of work

1. **Documentation.** State plainly in the profile-routing docs that profiles are a configuration and routing mechanism, not a trust boundary, and that a route secret authorizes *delivery*, not *identity*. Cheapest, and closes the expectation gap.
2. **Bind the secret to the profile.** Make the route secret profile-scoped so a secret issued for `A` is rejected on `B`'s path.
3. **Widen secret scoping** so credential reads consistently go through the profile-scoped accessor.

Happy to test any of these against a live multi-profile deployment.

### Environment

Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20), upstream `eb527605`, git install, Linux, `dispatch_in_gateway: true`.

This happens on hosts where git comes from a native MSYS2 mingw-w64

`C:\msys64\usr\bin\bash.exe`.

Root cause: the shell probe infers the install root from
`git --exec-path` by scanning the path for known prefix segments, but
**only `mingw32`/`mingw64` are recognised** — the prefixes Git for Windows
still uses, but which MSYS2 upstream has deprecated. **Modern MSYS2
toolchains live under `ucrt64` (the default `MSYSTEM`), `clang64`, and
`clangarm64`**, so a native git's exec path matches nothing and the root
cannot be inferred. Setting `KIMI_SHELL_PATH` works around it, but
auto-detection fails before any session starts, so session id and
context usage don't apply.

1. Windows host with MSYS2 installed at the default `C:\msys64`.

   `C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin` on PATH (do NOT install Git for Windows).
3. `git --exec-path` prints `C:/msys64/ucrt64/libexec/git-core`.
4. Launch kimi-code.

### What is the expected behavior?

Expected: detection resolves `C:\msys64\usr\bin\bash.exe` from the
git exec path. Actual: `KaosShellNotFoundError` as above.

TUI 流式文本在 Kimi 模型下显示卡顿 / 一跳一跳的

# TUI 流式文本在 Kimi 模型下显示卡顿 / 一跳一跳的

## 问题描述

在 `kimi-code` 的 TUI 中使用 **Kimi 模型** 时，助手回复的流式显示不够平滑，文字会明显“一跳一跳”地更新。同样的代码在 **DeepSeek 模型** 下就流畅很多。

同一个 Kimi 模型，在 [oh-my-pi](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi) 的 TUI 中流式输出是流畅的。这说明卡顿不是 Kimi API 本身的问题，而是 `kimi-code` 当前的渲染/flush 策略和 Kimi provider 的 delta 节奏不匹配。
> oh-my-pi 设置中的 `Smooth Streaming` 选项（已开启），其说明为 *"Reveal assistant text and streamed tool input smoothly while chunks arrive"*：
>
> ![oh-my-pi Smooth Streaming setting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chengkeen/chengkeen/master/issue-990-smooth-streaming-setting.png)


## 复现步骤

1. 启动 `kimi-code` 并使用 Kimi 模型（例如 `kimi k2.7 code`）。
2. 请求一个较长的 prose 回复，例如“给我讲讲这个代码库”。
3. 观察输出：字符以短而不规则的 bursts 出现，视觉上卡顿。
4. 切换到 DeepSeek 模型，使用同样的 prompt，输出明显更平滑。

## 原因分析

1. **固定 50ms flush 窗口**

   `apps/kimi-code/src/tui/constant/streaming.ts`：

   ```ts
   export const STREAMING_UI_FLUSH_MS = 50;
   ```

   第一个 delta 立即 flush，但后续 delta 必须等至少 50ms。Kimi provider 的 delta 间隔较长、每次内容较少，导致 UI 按 provider 的节奏“蹦字”显示。

2. **每次 flush 都重建 Markdown 组件**

   `apps/kimi-code/src/tui/components/messages/assistant-message.ts`：

   ```ts
   updateContent(text: string): void {
     this.contentContainer.clear();
     if (displayText.trim().length > 0) {
       this.contentContainer.addChild(new Markdown(displayText.trim(), 0, 0, createMarkdownTheme()));
     }
   }
   ```

   每次更新都 `clear()` 并 `new Markdown(...)`，导致 `pi-tui` 的缓存完全失效，每次都要对全文重新解析、重新折行。消息越长越卡。

3. **缺少平滑 reveal 层**

   当前 UI 直接显示当前累积的全部文本，没有动画层把不均匀的 delta 流转换成稳定帧率的逐字显示。Kimi 的 delta 节奏一不均匀，观感就是卡顿。

## 修复建议

参考 `oh-my-pi` 的做法：

1. **复用 Markdown 实例**

   在 `AssistantMessageComponent` 中不要每次 `updateContent` 都重建 `Markdown`，而是持有一个实例，只调用 `setText(fullText)`。`thinking.ts` 里已经这么做了，可以照搬。

2. **降低或自适应 flush 间隔**

   把 `STREAMING_UI_FLUSH_MS` 从 50ms 降到 20–30ms，或者改成自适应策略：delta 来得密集时合并，间隔较长时立即 flush。

3. **增加平滑 reveal 动画层**

   在 `StreamingUIController` 和 `AssistantMessageComponent` 之间加一个 `StreamingRevealController`：

   - 维护一个已显示的 grapheme 计数。
   - 以固定 30fps 逐帧推进。
   - 每帧至少推进几个字符，最多推进剩余未显示字符的 1/8。
   - 消息结束时（`message_end`）再一次性显示完整文本并做语法高亮。

   这样不管 API 多久来一个 delta，TUI 都按自己的节奏平滑显示。

4. **流式渲染跳过同步语法高亮**

   给流式中的渲染加一个 `transient` 标记，最终消息到达前不做同步 `highlightCode`，结束时再补一次完整渲染。

## 参考实现

- `oh-my-pi-main/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/controllers/streaming-reveal.ts`
- `oh-my-pi-main/packages/coding-agent/src/modes/components/assistant-message.ts`
- `oh-my-pi-main/packages/tui/src/components/markdown.ts`

## 相关代码

- `apps/kimi-code/src/tui/components/messages/assistant-message.ts`
- `apps/kimi-code/src/tui/components/messages/thinking.ts`
- `apps/kimi-code/src/tui/controllers/streaming-ui.ts`
- `apps/kimi-code/src/tui/constant/streaming.ts`

`kimi web` starts MCP servers from the CLI installation directory, breaking workspace-relative MCP tools

### What version of Kimi Code is running?

0.18.0

### Which open platform/subscription were you using?

kimi-code

### Which model were you using?

kimi-k2.7 thinking

### What platform is your computer?

win11 X64

### What issue are you seeing?

## Summary

When launching a session via `kimi web`, Kimi Code CLI spawns the MCP server process from its own installation directory (`~/.kimi-code/server`) instead of the user's current project directory. Any MCP server that derives its workspace/storage path from `process.cwd()` at startup ends up writing data to a server-side workspace rather than the project workspace.

Session-context tools still work because they resolve the active session at request time using runtime `process.cwd()` plus the cached `sessionMappings`, but storage-oriented tools (memory, notes, etc.) are misrouted.

## Root Cause

`mcp-server.js` computes its workspace at module-load time:

```js
const cwd = process.cwd();
function computeWorkspaceId() {
  const hash = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(cwd).digest('hex').slice(0, 8);
  return `workspace-${hash}`;
}
const workspaceId = computeWorkspaceId();
const storeRoot = path.join(__dirname, 'store', workspaceId);
```

- With local `kimi` launched from the project directory, `cwd` is the project directory → correct workspace.
- With `kimi web`, the same server process is started from `~/.kimi-code/server` → `cwd` becomes the server directory → wrong workspace (`workspace-<server-hash>` instead of `workspace-<project-hash>`).

The session-discovery code path avoids this because it calls `process.cwd()` on each request and looks up `sessionMappings` in `mcp-config.json`, but storage code paths do not re-evaluate the workspace.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create or install an MCP server whose workspace/storage directory is derived from `process.cwd()` at startup (e.g., a memory MCP that stores files under `store/workspace-<cwd-hash>/`).
2. Register it with Kimi Code CLI.
3. In a project directory, run:
   ```bash
   cd /path/to/your/project
   kimi web
   ```
4. In the web UI, perform an action that writes data through the MCP server (e.g., `remember` a note).
5. Observe where the data is actually saved:
   - **Expected**: `~/.kimi-code/tools/<mcp>/store/workspace-<project-hash>/...`
   - **Actual**: `~/.kimi-code/tools/<mcp>/store/workspace-<server-hash>/...`

### What is the expected behavior?

## Expected Behavior

MCP servers spawned by `kimi web` should operate within the context of the project from which `kimi web` was launched, so that workspace-relative storage and memory behave identically to local `kimi`.

## Actual Behavior

MCP servers spawned by `kimi web` operate within the Kimi CLI installation directory, causing workspace-relative storage to land in a server-level workspace and be isolated from the project.

### Additional information

## Environment

- OS: Windows / macOS / Linux (affected on all platforms)
- Kimi Code CLI version: observed on current `kimi web` behavior
- Launch mode: `kimi web`
- MCP server type: any server that derives workspace from `process.cwd()` at startup

## Suggested Fixes

1. **Start MCP servers from the project directory** (preferred): when `kimi web` launches an MCP server, set the child process's cwd to the project directory rather than the server installation directory.
2. **Pass the project directory explicitly**: expose an environment variable (e.g., `KIMI_PROJECT_DIR`) or initialization parameter so MCP servers can route storage correctly without relying on `process.cwd()`.
3. **Include workspace context in every tool call**: add `workspaceId` or `projectPath` to each `tools/call` request, allowing the server to resolve storage per request.

## Additional Context

This issue is particularly problematic for MCP servers that implement persistent memory or automatic context loading. Users building such tools expect that running `kimi web` in a project directory behaves like running `kimi` in the same directory, but the workspace mismatch breaks that assumption.

Mid-turn user message interrupts/detaches running delegation subagent

## Symptom
When a user sends a mid-turn message to a desktop/TUI Hermes session that currently has a background delegation () in flight, the subagent processing silently detaches. The subagent never returns its result to the parent conversation. Process check shows no active background agent; delegation summary file is never written.

This has now been reproduced twice in the same session with different model backends (first with , then  / ). The second dispatch after a mid-turn message did complete once Hermes re-dispatched, suggesting the race is between the user-message delivery and the async delegation completion handler.

## Expected
Mid-turn user delivery should not kill a running subagent. Either the subagent should finish and its result should be appended to the conversation as a new message, or it should be explicitly cancelled with a clear error — not silently dropped.

## Actual
Subagent disappears. No summary file. No completion notice. No error. Parent is left guessing whether the subagent is still running or failed.

## Environment
- Hermes Agent, desktop/TUI session
- Model: stepfun/step-3.7-flash:free / provider nous
- Delegation model: neuralwatt/glm-5.2-short-fast-flex
- Config delegation.max_concurrent_children: 3, max_spawn_depth: 1

problem_statement:
# Bug: HTTP 429 error record persists in session context and cannot be cleared

## Describe the bug

When Hermes receives an HTTP 429 (rate limit) from an upstream provider during a conversation, the error message "API call failed after 3 retries: HTTP 429" gets permanently stuck in the session context. Even after switching to a different working provider, this error message reappears on every subsequent user turn within the same session. The only way to clear it is /reset or restarting Hermes entirely.

## To Reproduce

1. Use a rate-limited third-party provider (e.g., a proxy that returns 429)
2. Send a message → Hermes shows "API call failed after 3 retries: HTTP 429"
3. Switch to a working provider (official DeepSeek, Claude, etc.)
4. Send another message in the same session
5. The 429 error reappears again and again

## Expected behavior

- Error messages from old failed API calls should not pollute subsequent turns
- Session should recover automatically when user switches to a working provider
- Or there should be a command to clear only the error records without resetting the whole session

## Workaround

Only /reset or restarting Hermes clears it, but this loses the conversation flow.

## Environment

- Hermes: v0.18.2
- macOS 15.5
- Interface: Desktop App / WeChat bot

problem_statement:
[Bug] codex app-server: MCP tool call_id exceeds Responses API 64-char limit — permanently bricks session (sibling of #10788)

## Symptom

Every request in a gateway session fails with a non-retryable HTTP 400 once any MCP tool has been called:

```
Invalid 'input[2].call_id': string too long. Expected a string with maximum length 64, but got a string with length 84 instead.
```

The failure is permanent for the life of the session. The offending item sits near the head of the transcript (`input[2]`), so every subsequent turn replays it and fails identically. Observed 8+ times across two sessions in a single day.

## Root cause

The codex app-server namespaces MCP tool call ids as `codex_mcp__<server>__<tool>_<codex_call_id>`. The `<codex_call_id>` component is either `call_<24 chars>` (30 chars) or `exec-<uuid4>` (41 chars). Hermes forwards this verbatim as `call_id` in the Responses API payload, where the limit is 64.

Budget arithmetic for the `exec-<uuid>` form:

```
64 - len("codex_mcp__") - len(server) - len("__") - 1 - 41  =  9
```

i.e. `len(server) + len(tool)` must be <= 9 combined. With the built-in `hermes-tools` server (12 chars) that is unsatisfiable — **every** Hermes tool routed through the MCP bridge overflows in that form.

Grouped from `~/.hermes/sessions/request_dump_*.json` (n=1162 call_ids across 9 dumps):

| count | max len | call_id shape |
|------:|--------:|---|
| 60 | 84 | `codex_mcp__codex_apps__google_drive.search_exec-<uuid>` |
| 24 | 77 | `codex_mcp__hermes-tools__web_search_exec-<uuid>` |
| 6 | 73 | `codex_mcp__hermes-tools__browser_get_images_call_*` |
| 28 | 72 | `codex_mcp__codex_apps__google_drive.search_call_*` |
| 34 | 71 | `codex_mcp__hermes-tools__browser_navigate_call_*` |
| 8 | 66 | `codex_mcp__hermes-tools__web_extract_call_*` |
| 4 | 65 | `codex_mcp__hermes-tools__web_search_call_*` |
| 902 | 52 | `codex_exec_exec-<uuid>` (native, fine) |
| 40 | 47 | `codex_apply_patch_call_*` (native, fine) |
| 90 | 40 | `codex_exec_call_*` (native, fine) |

Only MCP-routed tools overflow; native codex tools stay well under.

## Why it is unrecoverable in practice

Two aggravating factors observed on the same deployment:

1. The poisoned entry lands early in the transcript and `compression.protect_first_n` keeps the head verbatim, so it is among the last things evicted.
2. When compression is unavailable the transcript never shrinks at all, so the bad `call_id` is replayed forever. The only user-visible recovery is `/reset`, which discards the whole conversation.

Each 400 also aborts the turn and injects the "IGNORE those pending results" system note, so work completed during the failed turn is discarded — from the user's side this reads as the agent forgetting what it was doing.

## Relation to #10788

#10788 (closed) is the same class of defect on a sibling field: reasoning-item `input[*].id` exceeding the same 64-char limit, fixed by validating length before replay. `call_id` was not covered by that fix. The `codex_mcp__` prefix is constructed by the codex app-server rather than by Hermes, but as in #10788 Hermes is the component that builds and sends the payload and can sanitize before transmit.

## Suggested fix

Apply the #10788 treatment to `call_id`: before sending, if a `call_id` exceeds 64 chars, replace it with a stable shortened surrogate (e.g. `mcp_` + first 8 chars of a hash of the original), applying the identical rewrite to both the `function_call` and its matching `function_call_output` so the pairing survives. A one-line length guard at payload-build time would also convert this from a hard 400 into a recoverable condition.

Codex (OpenAI Responses) provider hits 400 "string_above_max_length" on multi-turn — reasoning item `id` exceeds 64-char limit

## Symptom
Any multi-turn conversation using the codex / OpenAI Responses provider fails with HTTP 400 after a few turns:

```
Invalid 'input[7].id': string too long. Expected a string with maximum length 64, but got a string with length 408 instead.
```

## Root cause
When Hermes replays prior-turn reasoning items back into the next request (for reasoning-chain continuity), it preserves whatever `id` was returned on the previous turn. With the codex backend, that `id` can be a 408-character opaque blob (same length/shape as `encrypted_content`). OpenAI's Responses API validates `input[*].id` at max 64 chars and rejects the request.

Observed: every reasoning item in a stuck conversation has `id_len == 408`, identical shape across items (i.e., not a normal short `rs_...` id). In one failing request with 29 input items, items `[7], [12], [16], [20]` were all `type: reasoning` with 408-char ids.

## Where in code
`run_agent.py` around lines 3966–3981 (response-item capture) and 3696–3710 (replay path). Both preserve `id` verbatim without length validation.

```python
# run_agent.py:3966
encrypted = getattr(item, "encrypted_content", None)
if isinstance(encrypted, str) and encrypted:
    raw_item = {"type": "reasoning", "encrypted_content": encrypted}
    item_id = getattr(item, "id", None)
    if isinstance(item_id, str) and item_id:
        raw_item["id"] = item_id   # <-- 408-char id gets stored
    ...
```

## Suggested fix
One of:
- (a) Drop `id` on replay when it exceeds 64 chars (keep `encrypted_content` + `summary`, which are what the API needs for reasoning-chain continuity).
- (b) Only pass through `id` when it matches the expected short-id pattern (e.g., `rs_...`).
- (c) Truncate/hash it to ≤64 chars.

(a) seems safest — the server regenerates/derives identity from `encrypted_content` on replay anyway.

## Repro
- Provider: `codex` (via CCS proxy at `http://127.0.0.1:8317/api/provider/codex`, model `gpt-5.4`)
- Start a multi-turn conversation with tool use
- After a few turns, every subsequent request 400s with the error above

## Workaround
`/clear` (drop history) — works because a fresh session has no reasoning blocks to replay.

## Environment
- Hermes main @ 4610551d
- CCS 6.9.23-0-plus
- Platform: macOS (darwin 25.4.0)
